packet.headline_seed: Trump to cheer on Knicks at NBA Finals game in New York City
packet.description_seed: The Knicks' stunning winning streak has energised the city as the New York basketball team prepares for the third game of the finals series at its home arena.

what: Trump to cheer on Knicks at NBA Finals game in New York City

clean_source_blocks.text: The Knicks' stunning winning streak has energised the city as the New York basketball team prepares for the third game of the finals series at its home arena.

Heightened security, a strict no-bag policy and airport-style screening will greet fans, as US President Donald Trump attends a pivotal NBA Finals game on Monday evening in New York City. The New York Knicks will clash with the San Antonio Spurs for game three of the finals - the first on their home turf of Madison Square Garden (MSG). The Knicks, appearing in their first finals since 1999, hold a 2-0 lead in the best-of-seven series, fuelling championship fever across the city. The hottest ticket in town is drawing Mayor Zohran Mamdani as well as Trump. A parade of celebrities have been spotted at other recent games, including actors Timothée Chalamet and Ben Stiller, and filmmaker Spike Lee.

WASHINGTON – President Donald Trump has openly trashed the NBA as a bastion of player activism with overt liberal politics that could “destroy” the game of basketball. And he’s deeply unpopular in New York City, with a historically low job approval rate. So why is he planning to attend Monday’s Game 3 finals matchup between the New York Knicks and San Antonio Spurs, the first in Madison Square Garden in 27 years? To steal a phrase from former President Bill Clinton, “It’s the politics, stupid.” The game between the Spurs and their 7’4” superstar center/power forward Victor Wembanyama and the Knicks, in their first NBA Finals since 1999, promises to be among the most watched televised NBA games in recent memory.

This season has represented a stunning reversal of fortunes for the Knicks after decades as one of the worst teams in the league. Now with a 2-0 lead in the finals, they need to win just two more games, out of a possible seven, to win the national championship for the first time since 1973. And the mood across New York City is electric. From the Empire State Building to One World Trade Center, skyscrapers have been lighting up the city's skyline orange and blue - the Knicks' team colours. A subway station near Madison Square Garden has been given a Knicks-themed makeover, and businesses across New York City's five boroughs are offering meal deals and special orange-and-blue ice-cream and bagels.

[Lähde: USA TODAY]
WASHINGTON – President Donald Trump has openly trashed the NBA as a bastion of player activism with overt liberal politics that could “destroy” the game of basketball. And he’s deeply unpopular in New York City, with a historically low job approval rate.

So why is he planning to attend Monday’s Game 3 finals matchup between the New York Knicks and San Antonio Spurs, the first in Madison Square Garden in 27 years?

To steal a phrase from former President Bill Clinton, “It’s the politics, stupid.”

The game between the Spurs and their 7’4” superstar center/power forward Victor Wembanyama and the Knicks, in their first NBA Finals since 1999, promises to be among the most watched televised NBA games in recent memory.

And while Trump is much more aligned with the pro-MAGA Ultimate Fighting Championship crowd, he’s likely going because it presents him with yet another opportunity to build his brand and be seen by more than 10 million people watching at home, presidential historian Matt Dallek told USA TODAY June 5.

“He loves attention. He loves eyeballs on him and being at the center of everything,” Dallek said. “And even though he decamped and moved to Florida, he still identifies in many ways as a New Yorker.”

“The Knicks being in the finals for the first time in many decades is a chance for him to kill two birds with one stone,” Dallek said. “He can generate some controversy. He can put all eyes on him, and he can bask in the reflective glory of the New York Knicks, even if he's getting booed or heckled.”

Trump has already attended multiple sporting events in the first 18 months of his second term, analysts say.

That includes numerous golf events and championships, Super Bowl LIX in New Orleans, the College Football Playoff National Championship in Miami, the Daytona 500 auto race, the U.S. Open Men’s Final in tennis, the FIFA Club World Cup Final and even the NCAA Wrestling Championships.

Trump is especially fond of attending UFC fight nights and matches with members of his Cabinet and inner circle. An octagon arena is near completion on the South Lawn of the White House for the UFC fight on his birthday.

Even President Barack Obama, a huge basketball fan, enjoyed a close relationship with the NBA and attended games − but never the NBA finals.

payload.title: Trump saapuu seuraamaan Knicksin finaali-iltaa New Yorkissa
payload.summary: New York Knicks pelaa NBA-finaalien kolmannen ottelun kotikentällään Madison Square Gardenissa maanantai-iltana. Presidentti Donald Trumpin odotettu läsnäolo kiristää turvatoimia, kun kaupunki elää joukkueen vahvaa pudotuspelikevättä.
payload.content:
Yhdysvaltain presidentti Donald Trumpin on määrä osallistua maanantai-iltana New Yorkissa pelattavaan NBA-finaalien kolmanteen otteluun, jossa New York Knicks kohtaa San Antonio Spursin Madison Square Gardenissa. Knicks johtaa paras seitsemästä -finaalisarjaa otteluvoitoin 2–0, ja kaupungissa on nähty poikkeuksellista koripallohuuman nousua joukkueen palattua finaaleihin ensimmäistä kertaa sitten vuoden 1999.

## Turvatoimet kiristyvät Madison Square Gardenissa

Otteluun saapuvia katsojia odottavat tehostetut turvajärjestelyt. Paikalla on määrä olla lentokenttätyyppinen turvatarkastus, ja areenalla noudatetaan tiukkaa laukkukieltoa. Trumpin läsnäolo lisää ottelun poliittista ja julkista painoarvoa, sillä kyseessä on jo valmiiksi yksi finaalisarjan seuratuimmista illoista.

Trump on aiemmin arvostellut NBA:ta ja liittänyt sarjan pelaaja-aktivismiin sekä liberaaliin politiikkaan. Hänen suosionsa New Yorkissa on kuvattu heikoksi, mikä tekee osallistumisesta huomionarvoista myös kaupungin poliittisen ilmapiirin kannalta. Ottelua seuraamaan odotetaan myös New Yorkin pormestaria Zohran Mamdania.

## Knicks-huuma näkyy koko kaupungissa

Knicksin kausi on merkinnyt jyrkkää suunnanmuutosta seuralle, jota on pitkään pidetty yhtenä liigan heikoimmista. Nyt joukkue on kahden voiton päässä mestaruudesta, joka olisi sille ensimmäinen sitten vuoden 1973.

New Yorkin tunnelma on näkynyt kaupunkikuvassa. Empire State Building ja One World Trade Center ovat loistaneet Knicksin oransseissa ja sinisissä väreissä, Madison Square Gardenin lähellä sijaitseva metroasema on saanut joukkueaiheisen ilmeen, ja eri puolilla kaupungin viittä hallintoaluetta yritykset ovat tarjonneet teemaan sopivia ruoka-annoksia, jäätelöitä ja bageleita.

## Ottelussa on urheilullista ja julkista latausta

Finaalisarjan kiinnostusta kasvattaa myös San Antonio Spursin tähtipelaaja Victor Wembanyama. Ottelun arvioidaan keräävän erittäin suuren televisioyleisön, ja aiemmissa peleissä katsomoissa on nähty useita tunnettuja henkilöitä, kuten Timothée Chalamet, Ben Stiller ja Spike Lee. Knicksille maanantai-illan kotiottelu on mahdollisuus vahvistaa otettaan finaalisarjasta ja siirtyä enää yhden voiton päähän mestaruudesta.
summary_bullets: Donald Trumpin on määrä seurata Knicksin ja Spursin NBA-finaaliottelua New Yorkissa.
Madison Square Gardenissa otetaan käyttöön tehostetut turvatoimet ja tiukka laukkukielto.
Knicks johtaa finaalisarjaa 2–0 ja tavoittelee ensimmäistä mestaruuttaan sitten vuoden 1973.

WASHINGTON – President Donald Trump has openly trashed the NBA as a bastion of player activism with overt liberal politics that could “destroy” the game of basketball. And he’s deeply unpopular in New York City, with a historically low job approval rate. So why is he planning to attend Monday’s Game 3 finals matchup between the New York Knicks and San Antonio Spurs, the first in Madison Square Garden in 27 years? To steal a phrase from former President Bill Clinton, “It’s the politics, stupid.” The game between the Spurs and their 7’4” superstar center/power forward Victor Wembanyama and the Knicks, in their first NBA Finals since 1999, promises to be among the most watched televised NBA games in recent memory.

This season has represented a stunning reversal of fortunes for the Knicks after decades as one of the worst teams in the league. Now with a 2-0 lead in the finals, they need to win just two more games, out of a possible seven, to win the national championship for the first time since 1973. And the mood across New York City is electric. From the Empire State Building to One World Trade Center, skyscrapers have been lighting up the city's skyline orange and blue - the Knicks' team colours. A subway station near Madison Square Garden has been given a Knicks-themed makeover, and businesses across New York City's five boroughs are offering meal deals and special orange-and-blue ice-cream and bagels.
